R2.passage: Most people think a desert is hot and sandy, but that is only half the story. The Atacama Desert in Chile is hot and dry, and it only rains a few times a year. It lies between mountains, so it is sometimes rainy on the mountains while the desert stays dry. Antarctica is the opposite: it is the coldest place on Earth and it is covered in ice. Yet it also has very little rain, so scientists call it a desert too. In the end, a desert is about water, not temperature.

R3.passage: Most people think a desert is hot and sandy, but that is only half the story. The Atacama Desert in Chile is hot and dry, and it only rains a few times a year. It lies between mountains, so it is sometimes rainy on the mountains while the desert stays dry. Antarctica is the opposite: it is the coldest place on Earth and it is covered in ice. Yet it also has very little rain, so scientists call it a desert too. In the end, a desert is about water, not temperature.

R4.passage: Antarctica is very cold. There is a lot of ice, but it doesn't rain a lot. So, Antarctica is a desert, too. It is hard for people, animals and plants to live in Antarctica because it is so cold there. Antarctica is also the windiest place on Earth: winds can travel at more than 300 kilometres an hour. Few plants can grow, and the animals that live there, like penguins, spend most of their time in the sea, where it is warmer and there is food.
